conventions.axes: Unity axes, metres. Unity x = -Blender x, Unity y = Blender z (up), Unity z = -Blender y. Assumes the kit FBX files are imported with Bake Axis Conversion so each kit object's local axes are Unity axes.
conventions.groups: Pieces that share kit object and material are grouped. Each instance is [object, position, rotation_euler_deg, scale, placement], the KEY POSE (before any motion channel). group.motion lists the same objects in the same order.
conventions.instance.rotation_euler_deg: Unity Euler angles in degrees (Quaternion.Euler(x, y, z)), rounded to 1 degree.
conventions.instance.position: Metres, rounded to 1 mm: the piece's pivot (its base centre, the kit convention; the sword, dagger, funnel and whirl bands, rays and soft rays pivot at their origin: the guard, or the axis foot).
conventions.instance.scale: A number for uniform scale, else [x, y, z] in Unity local axes.
conventions.group.kit_object: The object inside group.kit. A kit of enemy_model means a second skin of the enemy model itself (stone, black) shown over it in the given window; unity_shader_mockup means a shell to build as a shader on the real model.
conventions.group.material: The material the piece wears in the render (shared meshes are re-coloured per piece). Flat emission bands, as pass 2.
conventions.timing: animated. Every piece is keyed at 20 fps; time 0 is frame 7 (frames 1-6 are a 0.3 s lead-in), and each timeline ends with 0.5 s of settle.
conventions.motion: One entry per instance (same order): verb, visible [appear, vanish] s (a vanish of 9 or more means it stays), delay = appear time, duration, easing, and the channels: path = [[t, offset (Unity axes, world-aligned), easing into this key]], scale_keys = [[t, multiplier on the key-pose scale (Unity local x, y, z), easing]], spin = {axis (Unity), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied as Quaternion.AngleAxis(degrees, axis) * keyRotation about the pivot, orbit = {centre (Unity, from the origin), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied last about the vertical through the centre, follow_body = the body index whose motion the piece rides on. Before the first key a channel holds its first value, after the last its last. Easings: linear, out = 1-(1-x)^2, in = x^2, inout = smoothstep, outback = overshoot (c = 1.70158), step = jump at the key. Angles are in Unity's sense.
conventions.bodies: The enemy model (enemy_husk stand-in) per body with its own motion (path, scale_keys, spin, spin2 applied after spin); body 0 is the one the reaction lands on. The stand-ins face the player.
conventions.lights: None: every look is unlit beyond the scene sun.
conventions.ribbons: Curve ribbons (wind curls, lightning arcs, floor combs, chains of light) are not kit meshes: each lists its points (Unity axes, metres, relative to its centre), width_m, radius_profile (taper = thin tail to full head scaled by taper_tail_head; needle = thin at both ends; flat = even), material and ink. Build them as a tube or flat ribbon along the points with the ink outline.

verbs.ribbon_draw: draw_on = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is drawn from tail to head (the head leads). erase = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is wiped from the tail toward the head. Visible length = draw_on - erase; nothing pops in or out.
verbs.orbit: centre (player, station or body n), radius (m), turns_per_second (Unity sense, + = counter-clockwise from above), start (s), rise (m per s), and optional angle_keys added on top. The ribbon turns about the vertical axis through its centre from start.
verbs.spiral: an orbit with rise > 0: the ribbon climbs while it turns.

conventions.scale: Stand-in enemies are 1.89 m tall, the size of the castle soldiers. Pieces were drawn to read at the game camera (12.7 m); keep their size relative to the body in game, not to the screen.
conventions.source: staging/blender/2026-11-21_strikes/strikes.blend, scene ST, one station per dash look (x from 60000, 40 m apart, in the order earth, ice, fire, water, lightning, metal, life, dark, poison, light, wind). Built by script (dash/tools/dash_specs.py) from the elements 2, 3 and 4 kits, combo kit v3 and the arc strikes kit vfx_strikes_kit.fbx. No new meshes: there is no dash kit file.
conventions.made: 2026-11-21 by Claude through the Blender MCP connection.
conventions.strike_shape: dash: the Twin Knives' infused strike, attack_knife_5 (Weapons.cs:358), the passing spin: a 0.12 s windup, then in its 0.08 s active window the player is carried 2.8 m (lunge 0.4 + Travel 2.4) through the target, cutting with both knives (Reach 2.0, 200 degrees), and arrives turned to face the target's back (PassThrough). Every element follows the dash path and the cross cut: an X of two crescents drawn over the target at 1.6 m, carried on 2 m past the end of the dash.
conventions.origin: Every position is relative to the PLAYER's ground point where the dash starts (y = 0). The dash runs along dash_direction (Unity axes; the renders turn the player and path 35 degrees toward the camera's right so the dash reads across the screen). Pieces with about_player (placement c) are laid along the dash from that start point (they do not ride the player); ribbons whose centre is player likewise; bodies carry their positions from it; ribbons whose centre is "body k" are relative to that body's ground point. player_motion gives the stand-in player's own path and turn. In game, turn the look so dash_direction is the player's facing when the dash starts.
conventions.dash_timing: The player passes distance x along the dash at t = 0.08 * x / 2.8 s; past the end the cross cut carries on at 10 m/s (to 4.8 m by about 0.28 s). Every streak segment is drawn as the player passes and wiped just behind it; knives_reach_s gives when the knives reach each struck body. In Unity key them off the dash itself, not a fixed delay.
conventions.instance.placement: g = on the ground, b = on or around a body, c = along the dash from where it starts.
conventions.carrier: Nothing stands in for the knives: nothing is drawn on the weapons. The stand-in player is moved through the dash and turned round in the renders (player_motion); it is not part of the look.
conventions.motion.body: The body (index into bodies) a piece belongs to, with about_body = its position from that body (Unity axes). Written from the pass's specs (dash/tools/dash_specs.py) by dash/tools/dash_assemble_recipe.py.
conventions.per_struck_enemy: motion.per_struck_enemy = true marks a piece that exists once for each enemy the knives actually hit, placed about_body from that enemy and timed from the moment they reach it; spawn one set per struck enemy and none on a miss. Bodies 0 to 2 are struck (one on the path, one each side within reach); body 3 is out of reach (missed_bodies) and has nothing drawn on it.
conventions.look_fields: Each look carries element, moment (infused), strike_shape (dash), weapon, dash, dash_direction, player_motion, owner, answer, look (in words), struck_bodies, missed_bodies, knives_reach_s and per_struck_enemy_pieces.
conventions.dark_outline: Dark's hands (vfxst_hand_big_open, vfxst_hand_big_grip: one rounded organic mesh each; material st_hand_small, near-black with a violet rim) were rendered with a violet outline on their outer silhouette (Freestyle line set InkHands, colour 0.42, 0.18, 0.7 linear, thickness 1.5). Each hand is one merged mesh, so the outline never traces joins between parts. In Unity give them an outline pass in that colour on the silhouette only. The dash's shadow wisps (vfxe2_cloud_a/_b in st_sl_shadow_smoke) take the same violet silhouette outline.
conventions.poison_veins: Poison's bruise, wound, vein web and sheen are ribbons whose points were snapped onto the stand-in body's surface and sunk into it so they lie flat on the skin (the bruise shows as a flat patch about 1.5 cm proud, the fine vessels as painted lines) and ride its motion (follow_body). In Unity build them as a decal or a vein and bruise mask in the enemy's shader that spreads from the wound with the same timing; nothing should stand out of the body.
conventions.colour: Materials are flat emission in linear colour (ramp ones shade by facing, centre to rim), except the toon stone, which is lit toon with the ink outline. Metal uses the blue-grey st_sl_glint, Poison the sickly-rimmed st_sl_venom, as in the slam, spin and thrust. Metal, Light and Lightning run above the soldiers' shoulders, as the owner asked for THRUST. No stop reaches pure white: the strip maker counts pure-white pixels in every strip frame (dash/white_check.json): every look is 0.
conventions.revisions: 2026-11-21. Dark, picked by the owner (DASH and LASH): one OPEN hand per struck enemy rising flat-palmed out of the shadow beside it, lying 20 degrees off the floor with its palm toward the game camera so the five fingers show, held open 0.3 s, then closing on the leg and tugging. Round 2 (this recipe), the owner: Ice, Lightning, Water, Wind, Life, Earth and Metal approved and unchanged (checked identical to round 1). Fire's cross cut is real flame tongues tearing along the two cuts; Dark has one hand per struck enemy, rising out of its own shadow; Poison's veins carry a sickly-green rim (st_sp_vein_rim) so they read at the game camera; Light has one clean glare per knife cut and a single flare, on the enemy the cuts cross. Round 1: dash/r1/.
